title: Validation scorecard (npm run validate:predictions) + tune alpha/shrinkage/MAD/hysteresis against S3
goal: Score computeItemStats' held-out prediction accuracy against S-17's seeded ground truth, print the working spec Sec12 per-cohort scorecard, and gate on overall S3 (n>=4 purchases) clearing >=70% -- tuning computeItemStats' constants only if a genuine defect is found by inspection of a specific failing cohort, never by loosening the seeder's jitter to make a number pass.
in_scope: scripts/validate-predictions.ts (npm run validate:predictions): loads env the same way as S-17's seeder (own supabase-js client, no server-only import), fetches DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID's catalog_items (id, canonical_name) and category default_prior_days, regenerates the same deterministic ItemDef[] via S-17's generateItemDefs() and joins by canonical_name to get each item's real catalog_item_id (errors out with a clear message if the join is incomplete -- i.e. seed:history hasn't been run), fetches each item's real stock_movements (type='purchase', ascending) from the DB.

Held-out methodology: for an item with k total purchase events, train on events[0..k-2] and hold out events[k-1]; call computeItemStats(trainEvents, config, {cadenceBucket:null, intervalEstDays:null}) directly (pure function, no persistence, no server-only import problem) with config.now = the last training event's occurredAt, config.categoryPriorDays = the item's assigned category's default_prior_days, config.perishabilityDays = the item's perishability_days, config.currentStockBase = the last TRAINING event's own qtyBase (i.e. 'just restocked one pack' -- not an arbitrary fraction; advisor-caught before implementation: currentStockBase=0.5*packSize collapses next_purchase onto a systematically-wrong ~0.5x-interval depletion estimate for every item with q>=0.70, because q~=1 makes next_purchase track depletion_date alone, and depletion_date = last + currentStockBase/dailyRate = last + 0.5*T when currentStockBase=0.5*pack and dailyRate~=pack/T), config.rateCorrection = 1 (no S-15 reconciliation loop involved in this harness -- pure stats accuracy only). Compare predictedNextPurchaseAt against the held-out event's actual occurredAt.

S3 inclusion gate: an item counts toward the headline S3 percentage only when it has >=4 TRAINING events (i.e. >=5 total events, since one is held out) -- 'after 4 purchases of an item' (working spec Sec3/Sec12) means the model has seen 4, not that 4 total events exist including the untrained held-out one.

Per-cohort scorecard printed in the working spec Sec12 table format (cohort, n, within+/-25%, bucket correct, mean abs err) plus an overall S3 (n>=4) line with PASS/FAIL vs the 70% threshold; process exits 1 if overall S3 < 70%.

bucket correct: predicted cadenceBucket compared against the item's ground-truth expected bucket, computed via lib/predictions/computeItemStats.ts's exported `_internal.thresholdBucket` applied to the item's TRUE interval at the held-out point (a fixed target for most cohorts; for the drifting cohort, the true interval at that point in the linear 7d->14d drift) -- reuses the shipped algorithm's own boundary constants (_internal.CADENCE_BOUNDARIES_DAYS) rather than a second hand-copied threshold table that could silently drift out of sync.

Cohort-specific qualitative checks beyond the shared table, matching each cohort's stated purpose in working spec Sec12's table (printed as supplementary pass-rate lines, not folded into the S3 percentage): high_variance -- confidence < 0.7 (not High) for a majority of items; outlier_injected -- the injected outlier interval is actually excluded by `_internal.rejectOutliers` when run on the item's raw training intervals (confirms the harness's outlier really is one, not just that the final bucket happened to match); cold_start -- confidence < 0.35 (Learning) for all items (informational only, no held-out test since n<4); perishable_implausible_rate -- predictedDepletionAt <= lastPurchasedAt + perishabilityDays holds for all items (checked on predictedDepletionAt only, per advisor: the shipped blendNextPurchase mixes q against the UNCLAMPED rate.depletionDate, so predictedNextPurchaseAt is not expected to respect the clamp -- if this looks like a real product defect once observed live, it is recorded as a finding in the ledger with a live repro, not silently 'fixed' under cover of this story's tuning mandate); qty_inconsistent -- dailyRateBase stays null (rate branch suppressed) for a majority of items.

Tuning protocol if overall S3 < 70%: (1) re-check the harness itself first (held-out arithmetic, the S3 n>=4 gate, category-prior/target mismatches -- a lognormal sigma=0.15 clean-periodic cohort should land ~85-90% within +/-25% on a correct harness, matching working spec Sec12's own 88% example; a large shortfall there is almost always a harness bug, not evidence the algorithm needs retuning); (2) only after ruling that out, adjust EWMA_ALPHA / the shrinkage denominator / OUTLIER_MAD_MULTIPLIER / HYSTERESIS_MARGIN in lib/predictions/computeItemStats.ts, and re-verify E-5's exact fixture values from .claude/epic-5/ledger.md (A5: bucket=weekly, confidence exactly 0.50, next purchase ~=day 28; A6: outlier rejected, stays weekly; A7: interval_est=23.33, confidence=0.25, bucket=unpredictable) via a throwaway tsx script before trusting any constant change, and record the change + re-verification in .claude/epic-6/ledger.md.
out_of_scope: Persisting scorecard results anywhere -- stdout only, run on demand.
Any change to lib/predictions/reconcile.ts (S-15's rate_correction reconciliation) -- config.rateCorrection is fixed at 1 throughout this harness.
acceptance: `npm run validate:predictions` prints the Sec12-format per-cohort scorecard and an overall S3 (n>=4 purchases, i.e. >=5 total events per item) line; overall S3 clears >=70%, or the specific shortfall and remediation are recorded in the ledger if the resolved cause is a genuine algorithmic gap rather than a harness defect.
invariants: Never persists to item_stats/item_stats_history -- computeItemStats is called directly and its return value only ever read, never written back (avoids any interaction with the nightly cron or on-commit trigger, both scoped to the real household anyway per S-17's invariants).

half_yearly and yearly clean_periodic items are structurally excluded (or near-excluded) from the S3 percentage, not a seeding bug: computeItemStats' own step-1 lookback caps purchase history to the trailing 24 months (lib/predictions/computeItemStats.ts's gatherEvents), so a true ~200-500 day cadence item can never accumulate >=5 events inside that window no matter how far back synthetic history is seeded -- documented as a known, spec-level tension between working spec Sec12's 'all cadence buckets' cohort goal and Sec5 step 1's window, resolved by including those buckets for bucket-assignment correctness (informational) while excluding them from the n>=4 S3 average.

Tuning (if it happens at all) touches only the four named constants and is re-verified against every E-5 acceptance fixture before being trusted -- this story does not get to silently redefine what 'confidence High' or 'weekly' mean for the rest of the app.
